gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Bluetooth LE itself held a keyboard to one report every 7.5 ms (133 Hz) until Core 6.2, so only the 2.4 GHz dongle or the cable can deliver the 1,000 Hz reports gaming expects.
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide.com and rottenwifi.com (both cited), plus official.deals/under-50, mechvibes.com and techgearden.com. mkbguide gives no wireless polling or latency figure at all. rottenwifi says only "Wired models are generally the safer latency choice for competitive gaming", with no number or reason. official.deals has no per-mode figures. mechvibes gives one maker figure (MonsGeek FUN60 Max, 8000 Hz on 2.4 GHz) and nothing for Bluetooth. techgearden has part of it for one board outside ChatGPT's picks: "Kisnt lists latency of 2ms wired, 5ms on 2.4GHz and 11ms on Bluetooth". None gives the Bluetooth SIG's 7.5 ms / 133 Hz floor or explains why the dongle is the mode that matters. It stops short of 3 because I could not open a maker's per-mode polling figure for any candidate (gamakay.com and atk.store returned HTTP 429 on every attempt).
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it: for anyone who games, a board under $50 must include the 2.4 GHz dongle, and Bluetooth is the mode for typing and device switching. It rules out Bluetooth-only versions of the same model names. Redragon's own store still describes a K530 with "Bluetooth 5.0" and a "Dual Mode Switch" between wireless and wired, beside the tri-mode K530 Pro at $49.99, which is likely what ChatGPT's "verify the exact revision" on the RK61 is about. For our rows (Gamakay TK101 at $47.99, NS68 tri-mode at $39.99), the page should state Gamakay's polling rate per mode before using this, and for the Hall effect NS68 whether rapid trigger and 8K hold on 2.4 GHz. I could not read those figures today.

findings.label: Minimum Bluetooth LE connection interval before Core 6.2
findings.source_title: How Bluetooth Shorter Connection Intervals will impact the next generation of wireless innovations (Bluetooth SIG blog, Avi Negrin, 01 May 2026)
findings.note: Bluetooth SIG's words: "the minimum Bluetooth LE connection interval was 7.5 ms with a resolution of 1.25 ms." A keyboard on Bluetooth LE can hand the host a report at most once per connection interval.

findings.label: Highest report rate that interval allows
findings.source_title: How Bluetooth Shorter Connection Intervals will impact the next generation of wireless innovations (Bluetooth SIG blog)
findings.note: Bluetooth SIG: "a 133 Hz update rate, achievable with a 7.5 ms interval, may not be sufficient" for latency-sensitive uses. Arithmetic: 1 / 0.0075 s = 133.3 reports per second. A 1,000 Hz dongle or cable reports every 1 ms, so the Bluetooth interval is 7.5 times longer.

findings.label: Report rate the Bluetooth SIG says gaming expects
findings.source_title: How Bluetooth Shorter Connection Intervals will impact the next generation of wireless innovations (Bluetooth SIG blog)
findings.note: Bluetooth SIG: "For gaming, consumers expect HID devices such as gamepads and mice to support report rates of 1 kHz or higher." The article names gamepads and mice; applying it to keyboards is our reading.

findings.label: New minimum interval with Shorter Connection Intervals (Core 6.2)
findings.source_title: How Bluetooth Shorter Connection Intervals will impact the next generation of wireless innovations (Bluetooth SIG blog)
findings.note: Bluetooth SIG: SCI "reduces the minimum connection interval for Bluetooth LE by a factor of 20, from 7.5 ms to just 375 μs" and enables "report rates of up to 2666 Hz for wireless HID use cases". This is a Core 6.2 feature. Redragon lists the K530 Pro's Bluetooth as 3.0/5.0, so that board stays on the 7.5 ms floor.
